# Writing a Friendly Neighbourhood Pet-Sitting Agreement with AI

By the end of this guide you'll have a clear, one-page pet-sitting agreement ready to share with your neighbor — covering duties, rates, medications and what happens if something goes wrong. It's for anyone who's ever asked a friend to feed the cat and wished they'd put it in writing. A quick heads-up: the AI can draft a clear agreement, but it isn't a lawyer — for high-stakes or commercial arrangements, get a real legal review.

## Before you start
- **An AI assistant account** — any of the big ones works (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Le Chat). Pick whichever you already use or have free access to.
- **A few minutes of notes** about your pet (name, age, medications), the sitter (name, contact), the dates, and the agreed pay.
- **Rough total time:** about 15–20 minutes for a first draft, much less if you've done one before.

## Step 1 — List what your agreement needs to cover
Grab a notebook or open a blank note on your phone. Before you touch the AI, spend a few minutes jotting down the basics you want in writing: your pet's name, type and age, any medical conditions or medications, the dates you'll be away, daily routines (feeding times, walks, play), the sitter's name, agreed pay, and what happens in an emergency (vet name, your phone, a backup person). If you don't know something yet, just write question marks — that's fine. The point is to give the AI something real to work with later.
💬 Example: "Bella, 6-year-old ragdoll cat. Needs insulin every 12 hours. Going away 15–22 March. Sitter is Jade from next door. $40 per day. Emergency vet: Animal Hospital, phone 555-0123."
If you'd rather skip the notes and dive straight in, that's OK too — but the more detail you give the AI, the less you'll need to fix afterwards. You'll know it worked when you have a simple list — even a messy one — that captures your pet's needs and the basic deal.

## Step 2 — Ask your AI assistant to draft a first version
Open the AI assistant you already use — ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Microsoft Copilot or Le Chat all work well. Sign in if needed, then start a new chat. In the message box, type a clear request: ask for a pet-sitting agreement, say it's informal and for a neighbor or friend, and paste in the notes from Step 1. Ask for plain English, short sentences, and sections like Pet Details, Duties, Schedule, Pay, Emergency Plan and Liability. Then press Enter or tap the send arrow.
💬 Example: "Please draft a friendly pet-sitting agreement for my neighbor looking after my cat while I'm away. Use plain English and short sentences. Include sections for: pet details, daily duties, payment, emergency plan and who pays vet bills. Keep it under one page."
If your app uses a different send button (paper-plane icon, "Submit" or just the Enter key) they all do the same job. On free plans the assistant may reply a little slower or with shorter answers — that's normal. You'll know it worked when the AI replies within seconds with a structured agreement, usually with clear headings.

## Step 3 — Add your own details and ask for tweaks
Read what the AI wrote and look for gaps: medication, how the sitter gets paid (cash, bank transfer, daily or at the end), and who pays the vet if something goes wrong. Reply in the same chat with the changes you want. Be specific — don't say "add more", say exactly what to add and where. Press Enter to send.
💬 Example: "Add a 'Medications' section saying Bella needs insulin every 12 hours and the sitter must watch for low blood-sugar signs. Change Payment to $40 per day, bank transfer on the last day. Clarify: if Bella needs a vet, the owner pays up to $500 first, then we split anything above that."
If your AI offers a "Regenerate" or "Try again" button, ignore it for now — typing your own follow-up usually gives cleaner results. You'll know it worked when the AI replies with a new version that includes your changes while keeping the rest of the agreement intact.

## Step 4 — Read it as if you were the sitter
Read the agreement again, this time pretending you've never met the pet and you're being asked to look after it for a week. Does anything feel unclear, missing or unfair? Ask the AI to rewrite any section that doesn't feel right. Common things to check: who has keys and when, what happens if the sitter can't make a visit, who's liable if the pet damages something, and where to find food and clean-up supplies.
💬 Example: "Rewrite Section 4 (Keys and Access) so the sitter gets keys on day one and returns them on the last day. Also add: if the sitter can't make a visit, they must call the owner at least 2 hours before, or arrange a backup."
If your AI starts repeating itself or going off-topic, click "New chat" and paste in the latest version of your agreement — a fresh conversation often gives cleaner answers. You'll know it worked when the agreement reads clearly from a stranger's point of view — no vague sentences, no missing pieces.

## Step 5 — Save, share and sign
Copy the final agreement into a plain document — Google Docs, Word or a simple text file works fine. Send a copy to your sitter (and keep one for yourself) so you both have the same version. If you want a small touch of formality, ask the AI to add a short signatures section at the bottom — a quick text reply saying "I agree" is enough for a friendly neighbor arrangement.
💬 Example: ask the AI: "Add a short 'Signatures' section at the bottom with two lines: 'Owner: ______ Date: ______' and 'Sitter: ______ Date: ______'. Keep it warm and friendly in tone."
If you're on your phone, you can screenshot the final agreement or share the chat link if your assistant supports it. You'll know it worked when both you and your sitter have the same copy saved, with names and dates added, ready for the arrangement to begin.

## Common mistakes
- **Letting the AI write the whole thing without checking.** First drafts often miss your specific details (medication, vet number, exact pay). Always read it back and add what's missing — that's what Step 3 is for.
- **Leaving the language too legal.** If the agreement reads like a court contract, ask the AI to "rewrite in plain English a 12-year-old could understand." Friendly neighbor agreements work best when both sides can read them easily.
- **Forgetting the emergency plan.** Pet illness and accidents don't wait. Make sure your agreement names a vet, includes your phone number, and says who pays first if bills stack up. Ask the AI to add this if it's missing.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** you can use the same approach any time you need a quick, written agreement with someone — house-sitting, lending tools, splitting bills with a flatmate. The AI gives you the structure; you bring the details.
- **For your business or work:** the same process works for client agreements, freelance contracts or simple service terms. Just swap the language and add your own sections.
- **If you're just getting started:** start with a one-page agreement for one trip. Once you've done it once, the second one takes about 10 minutes — most of the wording stays the same.

## Try it now
Open your favorite AI assistant, paste in this: "Draft a friendly pet-sitting agreement for a neighbor looking after my [your pet type] while I'm away. Include sections for pet details, daily duties, payment, emergency plan and who pays the vet. Keep it under one page in plain English." See what comes back — that's your starting point.
